s1.syndrome_frame: Acute progressive limb weakness with areflexia
salient_findings: Uniform weakness of the right upper extremity
Complete flaccid paralysis of the right arm
key_facts: 55-year-old right-handed man
No significant medical history
Presented with two days of worsening heaviness in his right arm
Denied gait difficulty, pain, sensory changes, or cranial symptoms
Had an upper respiratory illness three weeks earlier
Denied diarrhea or recent vaccinations
Blood pressure was 220/139 mm Hg
Afebrile and alert
Uniform weakness of the right upper extremity with 1+ reflexes
Left upper extremity and bilateral lower extremities had strength 5/5 with 2+ reflexes
Sensation was intact
Cranial nerves were normal
Urine toxicology, head CT, brain MRI, and cervical-spine imaging were unremarkable
Lumbar puncture showed 1 white blood cell, no red blood cells, and protein 33 mg/dL
Serum assay for botulinum toxin was negative

shortlist.label: Guillain-Barré Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Acute progressive limb weakness with areflexia, recent upper respiratory illness

shortlist.label: Acute Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyneuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid progression of weakness, areflexia, and absence of sensory changes

shortlist.label: Miller Fisher Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of limb weakness, areflexia, and recent upper respiratory illness

shortlist.label: Poliomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute flaccid paralysis, areflexia, and recent history of illness

shortlist.label: Botulism
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of weakness, areflexia, and cranial nerve involvement, although serum assay was negative

raw.rationale: The patient's progressive weakness, areflexia, and lack of sensory changes are consistent with Guillain-Barré Syndrome, an autoimmune disorder that often follows an upper respiratory illness.

rejected.label: Acute Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyneuropathy
rejected.why: This is another term for Guillain-Barré Syndrome, but Guillain-Barré Syndrome is more specific and commonly used.

rejected.label: Miller Fisher Syndrome
rejected.why: This variant of Guillain-Barré Syndrome typically presents with ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, and areflexia, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Poliomyelitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and lack of fever, as well as the negative serum assay for botulinum toxin and unremarkable imaging, make poliomyelitis less likely.

rejected.label: Botulism
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and negative serum assay for botulinum toxin, as well as the lack of cranial nerve involvement, make botulism less likely.
